questions.title: Can you play two balls in match play if you’re not sure of the rules?
questions.question: In match play, if you don’t know what rule to use, are you allowed to hit two balls and use both scores?

choices.text: Yes, you can always hit two balls in match play
No, you should talk with your opponent or ask a referee
Only if your marker says it's okay
Only if you are playing by yourself

questions.explanation: You can’t play two balls in match play. If you are not sure about a rule, you and your opponent decide what to do, or you can ask a referee to help.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A golf game where you try to win more holes than your opponent.
A person who helps players follow the rules in golf.

questions.teachingTip: Act out talking with an opponent when not sure of a rule, to show what to do instead of playing two balls.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids think you can always play two balls if there is a problem.
Some think their marker (scorekeeper) can say it’s okay to play two balls.

questions.title: Is playing two balls allowed in match play?
questions.question: If you’re playing match play and are not sure what the correct rule is for your situation, are you allowed to play two balls and count both scores?

choices.text: Yes, you can always play two balls in match play
No, you must work out the situation with your opponent or ask for a ruling
Only if your marker gives permission
Only if you are playing alone

questions.explanation: In match play, you are not allowed to play two balls. You and your opponent must agree what to do, or ask for a ruling from a referee if you can’t agree.
